title: How sky subtraction scales affect Intracluster light measurements
comment: 3 pages, 1 figure. Accepted for publication in RNNAS on 1 November 2026
summary: Deep imaging surveys are opening a new window on the low surface brightness universe. However, the recovery of diffuse emission depends on the survey depth and how the sky background is treated. Estimating the sky on scales comparable to astrophysical sources risks biasing flux measurements. This effect is particularly significant for intracluster light, the most extended diffuse baryonic component of galaxy clusters. We show in a $M_{500}$--$z$ plane that the sky subtraction scales employed in the Legacy Survey of Space and Time Data Preview 2 and Hyper Suprime-Cam Public Data Release 3 (HSC-PDR3) impact clusters with $M_{500}\gtrsim10^{13.4}\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$ at all redshifts, whereas HSC-PDR2 only oversubtracts the most massive systems at $z < 0.1$. The larger sky subtraction scale anticipated for the full LSST survey will mitigate this bias.

AI.tldr: Sky subtraction on scales comparable to astrophysical sources biases diffuse flux measurements, particularly for intracluster light; the sky subtraction scales used in LSST DP2 and HSC-PDR3 affect clusters with M500 ≳ 10^13.4 M_⊙ at all redshifts, while HSC-PDR2 only oversubtracts the most massive systems at z < 0.1.
AI.motivation: Deep imaging surveys enable study of the low surface brightness universe, but recovering diffuse emission depends on survey depth and sky background treatment. Estimating the sky on scales comparable to astrophysical sources risks biased flux measurements, an effect especially significant for intracluster light, the most extended diffuse baryonic component of galaxy clusters.
AI.method: The authors analyze the sky subtraction scales employed in LSST Data Preview 2 and HSC Public Data Release 3 (and compare with HSC-PDR2), mapping the impact of oversubtraction across the M500–z plane.
AI.result: The sky subtraction scales used in LSST DP2 and HSC-PDR3 impact clusters with M500 ≳ 10^13.4 M_⊙ at all redshifts, whereas HSC-PDR2 only oversubtracts the most massive systems at z < 0.1. The larger sky subtraction scale anticipated for the full LSST survey will mitigate this bias.
AI.conclusion: Sky subtraction scale is a critical systematic for diffuse intracluster light measurements; current survey pipelines bias massive-cluster fluxes, but the larger sky subtraction scale planned for the full LSST survey should reduce this bias.

title: CosmoVerse Data Challenge: How Tip of the Red Giant Branch Analysis Choices Shape the Inferred Hubble Constant
comment: 90 pages, 6 tables, 3 figures
summary: Tip of the red giant branch (TRGB)-based determinations of the Hubble constant ($H_0$), the current expansion rate of the Universe, depend on choices made in selecting and analyzing stellar photometry and in assembling the sample of calibrator galaxies hosting Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia). The CosmoVerse Data Challenge invites participants to analyze public photometric catalogs within a shared distance-ladder framework, opening each step of the measurement to the community and testing how these choices propagate into $H_0$. Participants independently selected photometric catalogs, galaxies, and TRGB measurement settings, while using a common SN Ia compilation and fitting procedure to convert distances into $H_0$. Supported by public notebooks and a training school, the challenge received 26 submissions from 22 participants. All submissions used the same analysis notebook, many participants were trainees at the school, and the true galaxy distances are unknown; the results therefore characterize the sensitivity of the submissions to analysis and sample-selection choices and are not a combined determination of $H_0$ or an estimate of the systematic uncertainty in published TRGB measurements. The inferred $H_0$ values have a median of $77.10\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and a standard deviation of $7.38\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ $(5.11\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ for the scaled median absolute deviation), $\sim 3.4$ $(\sim 2.4)$ times the typical quoted uncertainty of a submission. Differences in the measured tip of the anchor galaxy NGC 4258 add a coherent shift in the distance scale. The challenge shows how different choices within a common framework can produce substantially different values of $H_0$, and provides an open basis for tracing these differences and for making datasets and tools more transparent and accessible.

AI.tldr: A community data challenge shows that choices in TRGB photometry and calibrator-galaxy selection can shift H0 substantially, with submissions yielding a median of 77.10 km/s/Mpc and a scatter of ~7.4 km/s/Mpc.
AI.motivation: TRGB-based H0 determinations depend on many analyst choices—photometric catalog selection, galaxy sample, and TRGB measurement settings—whose propagation into H0 is not well characterized. The CosmoVerse Data Challenge aims to open each step of the distance ladder to community scrutiny and quantify how these choices affect H0.
AI.method: Participants independently chose photometric catalogs, calibrator galaxies, and TRGB measurement settings, but used a common SN Ia compilation and fitting procedure to convert distances into H0. Support was provided via public notebooks and a training school, yielding 26 submissions from 22 participants.
AI.result: Inferred H0 has a median of 77.10 km/s/Mpc with a standard deviation of 7.38 km/s/Mpc (5.11 via scaled MAD), roughly 3.4 (2.4) times the typical quoted per-submission uncertainty. Variation in the measured TRGB tip of anchor galaxy NGC 4258 induces a coherent shift in the distance scale.
AI.conclusion: Different choices within a common framework produce substantially different H0 values. Because distances are unknown, results characterize sensitivity to analysis and sample-selection choices rather than a combined H0 or a systematic-uncertainty estimate; the challenge provides an open basis for tracing differences and improving transparency of data and tools.

title: Searching for Signatures of i-process Nucleosynthesis in Metal-Rich, Lead-rich Barium Stars
comment: 18 pages, 7 figures, 7 tables. Submitted to MNRAS. Comments welcome
summary: The intermediate neutron-capture process ($i$-process) has been invoked to explain the peculiar compositions of carbon-enhanced metal-poor (CEMP) stars enriched in both slow- ($s$) and rapid- ($r$) neutron-capture elements. Recent literature has questioned its operation at higher metallicities, but observational evidence remains limited. We analyse Gemini/GHOST and McDonald/Tull spectra of six $\rm -0.7 < [Fe/H] < -0.1$ stars identified in GALAH by their extreme Ba and Eu (or Sm) compositions ($\gtrsim$10$\times$ solar). We also reanalyse archival spectra of two literature $i$-process candidates. We determine abundances in up to 42 elements (Li through Pb), $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C, and Mg isotopic ratios, and compare to literature barium and CEMP stars and multiple asymptotic giant branch (AGB) model grids. Three stars exhibit extreme [Pb/Fe] (+1.79$\pm$0.19 to +2.50$\pm$0.32 dex), and two extreme [Eu/Fe] (+1.10$\pm$0.11 to +1.30$\pm$0.11 dex), distinguishing them from typical metal-rich barium stars. Two of these three exhibit abundance patterns that are inconsistent with $s$-process models and best explained by existing $i$-process predictions. The remaining sample is either consistent with $s$-process enrichment or suggestive of atomic diffusion. Both literature candidates are well-fit by the $i$-process model, but conventional $s$-process enrichment cannot be excluded. Our findings reinforce that metal-rich AGB stars contribute to the production of elements classically attributed to the $r$-process. These results identify promising candidates for $i$-process enrichment near solar metallicity and motivate additional $i$-process models to understand the contribution of this nucleosynthetic process to the chemical evolution of the Milky Way disk.

AI.tldr: Gemini/GHOST and McDonald/Tull spectroscopy of six metal-rich stars with extreme Ba and Eu reveals that metal-rich AGB stars producing the intermediate neutron-capture process can synthesize elements classically attributed to the r-process, identifying promising i-process candidates near solar metallicity.
AI.motivation: The i-process has been invoked to explain CEMP stars enriched in both s- and r-process elements, but its operation at higher metallicities has recently been questioned, and observational evidence at such metallicities remains limited.
AI.method: The authors analyze Gemini/GHOST and McDonald/Tull spectra of six stars with -0.7 < [Fe/H] < -0.1 selected from GALAH for extreme Ba and Eu (or Sm) compositions (≳10× solar), plus reanalyze archival spectra of two literature i-process candidates. They derive abundances for up to 42 elements (Li through Pb), ^12C/^13C and Mg isotopic ratios, and compare against literature barium and CEMP stars and multiple AGB model grids.
AI.result: Three stars show extreme [Pb/Fe] (+1.79±0.19 to +2.50±0.32 dex) and two show extreme [Eu/Fe] (+1.10±0.11 to +1.30±0.11 dex), distinguishing them from typical metal-rich barium stars. Two of these three have patterns inconsistent with s-process models and best explained by i-process predictions. The remaining sample is consistent with s-process enrichment or suggestive of atomic diffusion. Both literature candidates are well-fit by the i-process model, though conventional s-process enrichment cannot be excluded.
AI.conclusion: Metal-rich AGB stars contribute to the production of elements classically attributed to the r-process. The results identify promising i-process candidates near solar metallicity and motivate additional i-process models to clarify this nucleosynthetic process's contribution to the chemical evolution of the Milky Way disk.

title: Dynamics of self-gravitating halos with decaying dark matter
comment: 11 pages, 9 figures. Comments welcome!
summary: We study the evolution of self-gravitating spherical dark matter halos composed of dark matter particles that decay to a slightly less massive particle and a massless particle. The small kick velocity imparted to the daughter particle upon decay heats the halo. If the kick velocity is small compared with the characteristic velocity, the halo remains bound but puffs out. We also consider, for the first time, decaying halos with anisotropic initial conditions and find non-negligible effects on the resulting density profile. To simulate the halo evolution, we utilize the recently developed \texttt{NSphere} code across a broad range of decay times and kick velocities. We train an emulator to provide a mapping between the decay parameters and the relaxed density profile. We discuss how the resulting halo-scale signatures complement existing cosmological constraints on decaying dark matter and can be tested by upcoming surveys.

AI.tldr: The authors use the NSphere code to simulate the evolution of self-gravitating spherical dark matter halos whose particles decay into a lighter particle plus a massless particle, studying how the resulting "kick" heats and puffs out the halo, and they build an emulator mapping decay parameters to the relaxed density profile.
AI.motivation: Decaying dark matter is constrained mainly by cosmological observables, but its effects at the scale of individual halos are less explored. Understanding how decays modify relaxed halo density profiles—including contributions from anisotropic initial conditions—can provide complementary, halo-scale signatures testable by upcoming surveys.
AI.method: Simulate spherical self-gravitating dark matter halos with the recently developed NSphere code over a broad range of decay times and kick velocities. The decaying particle converts to a slightly lighter particle and a massless particle, imparting a small velocity kick that heats the halo; both isotropic and (for the first time) anisotropic initial conditions are considered. An emulator is trained to map decay parameters to the relaxed density profile.
AI.result: When the kick velocity is small compared with the characteristic velocity, the halo remains bound but expands ("puffs out"). Anisotropic initial conditions produce non-negligible effects on the resulting density profile. The emulator reproduces the mapping from decay parameters to relaxed density profiles across the studied parameter space.
AI.conclusion: Decaying dark matter imprints characteristic halo-scale signatures that complement existing cosmological constraints and can be probed by upcoming surveys, with anisotropic initial conditions mattering for accurate density-profile predictions.

title: Brewing another binary in the Teapot: Nandou=Phi Sagittarii
comment: 11 pages, 7 figures + Appendix
summary: The iconic Teapot asterism in Sagittarius is particularly rich in intermediate-mass stars in multiple systems. Here we combine VLTI/GRAVITY, archival spectroscopic observations, past radial velocity measurements and photometry to solve for the orbital and stellar parameters of the binary Nandou=Phi Sagittarii. It has a period $P=238.844\pm0.011$ days, a semi-major axis $a=1.32\pm0.10\text{ au}$ and eccentricity $e=0.418\pm0.004$. The precision in the dynamical masses $M_A=3.8\pm0.9 M_{\odot}$ and $M_B=1.6\pm0.4 M_{\odot}$ is currently limited by the parallax $p=12.5\pm1.0 \text{ mas}$. We find that the original Hipparcos 1997 Intermediate Astrometric Data (IAD) are consistent with the expected photocenter semi-major axis $a_{\mathrm{phot}} \sim 5 \text{ mas}$, while the IAD from the Hipparcos 2007 new reduction yield a too small $a_{\mathrm{phot}} = 1.7\pm0.3 \text{ mas}$, confirming the suspicion that a too aggressive modeling of the satellite attitude can lead to overfitting that suppresses the orbital motion. Matching the primary's temperature $T_{\mathrm{eff,A}} = 12000\pm250 \text{ K}$ and radius $R_{\mathrm{A}} = 5.1\pm 0.4 R_{\odot}$ to stellar evolutionary models implies that it is a $M_A \simeq 4 M_{\odot}$ star near the end of the main-sequence. Nandou will eventually most likely become a symbiotic star.

AI.tldr: Orbital and stellar parameters of the intermediate-mass binary Nandou (Phi Sagittarii) are derived by combining VLTI/GRAVITY interferometry, spectroscopy, radial velocities and photometry; the dynamical masses remain limited by parallax, and the original Hipparcos astrometry is shown to be consistent with the expected photocenter orbit while the 2007 re-reduction overfits and suppresses it.
AI.motivation: The Teapot asterism in Sagittarius is rich in intermediate-mass stars in multiple systems, yet precise dynamical masses and orbits for such binaries are scarce because they require combining high-angular-resolution astrometry with spectroscopy and radial velocities.
AI.method: Combination of VLTI/GRAVITY interferometric astrometry with archival spectroscopy, past radial velocity measurements and photometry to fit the orbital and stellar parameters of the binary Nandou = Phi Sagittarii; dynamical masses compared with temperatures and radii matched to stellar evolutionary models, and the Hipparcos 1997 IAD and 2007 new-reduction IAD compared against the expected photocenter orbit.
AI.result: Period P = 238.844 ± 0.011 d, semi-major axis a = 1.32 ± 0.10 au, eccentricity e = 0.418 ± 0.004. Dynamical masses M_A = 3.8 ± 0.9 M_sun and M_B = 1.6 ± 0.4 M_sun, limited by the parallax p = 12.5 ± 1.0 mas. The Hipparcos 1997 IAD agree with the expected photocenter semi-major axis a_phot ~ 5 mas, whereas the 2007 new reduction yields a_phot = 1.7 ± 0.3 mas, too small. The primary has T_eff,A = 12000 ± 250 K and R_A = 5.1 ± 0.4 R_sun, implying M_A ~ 4 M_sun near the end of the main sequence.
AI.conclusion: A precise orbit is established for Nandou, with dynamical masses still parallax-limited; the discrepancy between the two Hipparcos reductions confirms that overly aggressive satellite-attitude modeling can overfit and suppress orbital motion. Nandou will most likely evolve into a symbiotic star.

title: Euclid. Predicting scaling relations for emission-line galaxies using simulated data
comment: 12 pages, 9 figures, 5 pages appendix, submitted for publication to A&A
summary: The Euclid spectroscopic surveys will substantially increase the number of observed emission-line galaxies. We assess the ability of the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS) and Euclid Deep Survey (EDS), at the final DR3 depth, to recover the star-forming main sequence (MS), dust-mass relation (DMR), and mass-metallicity relation (MZR) from emission-line measurements. We use MAMBO (mocks with abundance matching in Bologna) spectroscopic simulations processed with the official Euclid pipelines. The MS is traced over $0\leq z\leq 4$ using Pa$β$, H$α$, and [OII] as SFR tracers. The shallow EWS flux limit biases the MS towards higher normalisation and a flatter slope by selecting the brightest, most strongly star-forming galaxies. The deeper EDS enables almost complete sampling with Pa$β$ and H$α$ at log$_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)\geq10.3$ over $0\leq z\leq 1.88$, with mild biases at both redshift limits. The [OII]-based MS is increasingly biased towards higher SFRs at the highest redshifts. The DMR is traced through the Balmer decrement over $1.45\leq z\leq 1.88$ and $0.9\leq z\leq 1.88$ in the EWS and EDS, respectively. The derived colour excess agree well with the input values, although detecting the faint H$β$ line restricts the sample to less obscured galaxies at fixed $M_*$, particularly in the EWS; the DMR is better sampled in the EDS. Finally, a golden sample detected in multiple optical rest-frame emission lines at $1.49\leq z\leq 1.88$ recovers gas-phase metallicities with typical accuracy of 0.1 dex at log$_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)\geq10$, while lower-mass galaxies show biases up to 0.15 dex. Relative to H-band limited sample, this sample preferentially traces the upper MS and lower MZR. Despite the simplified simulations lacking effects such as mutual spectral contamination and detector persistence, these forecasts provide a benchmark for future Euclid spectroscopic analyses.

AI.tldr: Using MAMBO mock simulations processed through official Euclid pipelines, the paper forecasts how well the Euclid Wide and Deep Surveys (at DR3 depth) can recover the star-forming main sequence, dust-mass relation, and mass-metallicity relation from emission-line measurements.
AI.motivation: Euclid spectroscopic surveys will dramatically increase the number of observed emission-line galaxies, so it is important to quantify the biases and limitations inherent to flux-limited samples when deriving fundamental scaling relations (MS, DMR, MZR).
AI.method: The authors use MAMBO (mocks with abundance matching in Bologna) spectroscopic simulations processed with the official Euclid pipelines. The MS is traced over 0≤z≤4 via Paβ, Hα, and [OII] as SFR tracers; the DMR is derived through the Balmer decrement; and metallicities are recovered from a multi-line "golden sample" at 1.49≤z≤1.88.
AI.result: The shallow EWS flux limit biases the MS toward higher normalization and flatter slope by selecting the brightest, most star-forming galaxies. The deeper EDS allows nearly complete sampling with Paβ and Hα at log10(M*/M⊙)≥10.3 over 0≤z≤1.88, with mild biases at the redshift limits; the [OII]-based MS becomes increasingly biased toward higher SFR at high z. DMR color excesses agree well with input values, though faint Hβ detection restricts the sample to less obscured galaxies at fixed M* (especially in EWS), with better sampling in EDS. The golden sample recovers metallicities to ~0.1 dex at log10(M*/M⊙)≥10, with biases up to 0.15 dex at lower masses, and preferentially traces the upper MS and lower MZR relative to H-band limited samples.
AI.conclusion: Despite simplified simulations that lack mutual spectral contamination and detector persistence, these forecasts provide a useful benchmark for future Euclid spectroscopic analyses of galaxy scaling relations.

title: The spatial structure of solar magnetoconvection at scales up to $60$~Mm
comment: 9 pages, 12 figures
summary: While convective motions at the scale of granules on the solar surface are well understood, those of mesogranular and supergranulation are not. At still larger scales, the lack of giant cells is a major mystery. We aim to slightly improve understanding of the radial and horizontal flows associated at mesogranular scales and supergranulation. We perform a deep MURaM small-scale dynamo simulation, extending from $50$~Mm below the solar surface and with a horizontal size of 60~Mm and sufficient resolution to begin to properly resolve the magnetic bright points in intergranular lanes. We determine the structure of the convective modes from the simulations at different scales, and compare the power spectra to those which have been previously observed. At all scales which are resolved by the simulation the simulated flows agree with the amplitude implied by Doppler measurements and local correlation tracking (LCT) measurements. The power in the vertical Doppler velocities at supergranular and larger scales is shown to be influenced by density perturbations near the surface. The structure of the modes at depth is simple as expected from the previous study of \cite{LordCameron2014} except the horizontal forcing scale scales like $H_ρ^{2/3}$ instead of $Hρ$. The simulations reproduce the observations up to scales of $60$~Mm. Within the simulated range, $l>=70$, we do not see the excess power associated with the convective conundrum.

AI.tldr: A deep MURaM small-scale dynamo simulation (60 Mm horizontal extent, from 50 Mm depth) reproduces observed vertical and horizontal convective flows up to scales of 60 Mm, including mesogranular and supergranular scales, and finds no excess power associated with the convective conundrum.
AI.motivation: Convection at granular scales is well understood, but mesogranular and supergranular scales are not, and the absence of giant cells at larger scales remains a major mystery. The authors aim to improve understanding of the radial and horizontal flows at mesogranular and supergranular scales.
AI.method: A deep MURaM small-scale dynamo simulation extending 50 Mm below the solar surface with a 60 Mm horizontal domain and sufficient resolution to begin resolving magnetic bright points in intergranular lanes. Convective mode structure is determined at different scales and power spectra are compared with previously observed Doppler and local correlation tracking (LCT) measurements.
AI.result: At all scales resolved by the simulation, the simulated flows agree in amplitude with Doppler and LCT measurements. Power in vertical Doppler velocities at supergranular and larger scales is influenced by near-surface density perturbations. The mode structure at depth is simple, as expected from prior work, except the horizontal forcing scale scales like H_rho^(2/3) rather than H_rho. No excess power associated with the convective conundrum appears for l >= 70.
AI.conclusion: The simulations reproduce observations up to scales of 60 Mm. Within the simulated range (l >= 70), the excess power associated with the convective conundrum is not seen, suggesting that the conundrum may lie at scales or depths not captured by this setup.

title: Euclid: Forecasting the number counts of bright line emitters in the Euclid Wide Survey and Euclid Deep fields
comment: 13 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to A&A
summary: The Euclid mission will revolutionize our understanding of the visible Universe by collecting images and spectra of millions of galaxies across cosmic time and environments. Here, we forecast the number counts of galaxies emitting [OII], H\b{eta}, [OIII], Hα and Pa\b{eta} lines in the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS) and Deep Survey (EDS). We compare predictions from different models, including semi-analytic models and empirical scaling relations. We then simulate spectra for galaxies in the MAMBO lightcone using FastSpec, designed to rapidly generate one-dimensional spectra as observed by Euclid. We process these simulated spectra with the official Euclid spectroscopic pipeline to recover redshifts and line fluxes and derive expected counts. Predictions for Hα+[NII] emitters are broadly consistent across mocks and with existing observations. In the EWS, relative RMS scatter among mock predictions for integrated counts is approximately 19% for Hα+[NII], 44% for [OII] and 41% for [OIII], reflecting greater model dependence for oxygen-line forecasts. After accounting for flux losses and redshift misidentification, corrected flux measurements recover most intrinsic line counts, especially in the EDS. From the MAMBO-based FastSpec simulations, we predict that Euclid will detect about 42 million Hα emitters in the EWS and 1.7 million in the EDS. The same simulations predict approximately 0.5 and 0.8 million [OII] and [OIII] emitters, respectively, in the EDS, and about 1.3 and 7.5 million in the EWS. These non-Hα forecasts remain subject to substantial model-dependent uncertainties, as shown by scatter among the different mocks. These samples will be instrumental in pushing large-scale structure and baryon acoustic oscillation studies beyond redshift z~2, extending Euclid cosmological and galaxy evolution studies beyond what is achievable with Hα alone.

AI.tldr: Forecasts galaxy emission-line number counts (Hα, [OII], [OIII], Hβ, Paβ) for the Euclid Wide and Deep Surveys using FastSpec simulations on the MAMBO lightcone, with results validated against observations and Euclid's spectroscopic pipeline.
AI.motivation: Euclid will image and spectroscopically survey millions of galaxies, but expected yields of key emission-line tracers beyond Hα (e.g., [OII], [OIII], Hβ, Paβ) are uncertain and model-dependent. Quantifying these forecasts is needed to plan cosmological and galaxy-evolution studies extending beyond z~2.
AI.method: Compares predictions from semi-analytic models and empirical scaling relations; simulates galaxy spectra in the MAMBO lightcone with FastSpec, producing Euclid-like 1D spectra; processes them through the official Euclid spectroscopic pipeline to recover redshifts and line fluxes and derive expected counts in the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS) and Deep Survey (EDS).
AI.result: Hα+[NII] predictions are consistent across mocks and with existing observations. Integrated-count RMS scatter among mocks is ~19% for Hα+[NII], 44% for [OII], and 41% for [OIII], indicating stronger model dependence for oxygen lines. After correcting for flux losses and redshift misidentification, most intrinsic counts are recovered, especially in the EDS. FastSpec/MAMBO predicts ~42M Hα emitters in the EWS and ~1.7M in the EDS; for [OII] ~0.5M (EDS) and ~1.3M (EWS); for [OIII] ~0.8M (EDS) and ~7.5M (EWS).
AI.conclusion: Euclid will deliver large samples of Hα, [OII], and [OIII] emitters, enabling large-scale structure and BAO studies beyond z~2 and extending cosmological and galaxy-evolution science beyond what Hα alone permits, though non-Hα forecasts carry substantial model-dependent uncertainties.

title: How fast is the fastest-rotating O-type star in the Galaxy?
comment: 6 pages, 1 figure and 2 tables, A&A Accepted
summary: {Rapid rotation distorts massive stars, making parameters from spherical models inclination-dependent. We studied these effects in the extreme Galactic O-type runaway LAMOST J040643.69+542347.8.} {We re-determined its stellar and rotational parameters with an oblate, gravity-darkened photospheric model and tabulated Stark profiles for selected \ion{He}{ii} lines.} {We fitted continuum-normalised spectra over 4000--4600\,Å with \texttt{ZPEKTR}, using TLUSTY/SYNSPEC emergent fluxes, limb darkening to weight their angular contribution over the visible Roche surface, Espinosa-Lara \& Rieutord gravity darkening, and Schöning--Butler Stark profiles. Interstellar and wind- or circumstellar-dominated features were masked.} {The model reproduces \ion{He}{ii}~$\lambda4200$, \ion{He}{i}~$\lambda4471$, and \ion{He}{ii}~$\lambda4542$. We obtained parent non-rotating counterpart (PNRC) parameters $T_{\rm eff}^{\rm PNRC}=38\,716\pm1041$~K, $\log g^{\rm PNRC}=4.12\pm0.12$, and $v_{\rm e}\sin i=587\pm73$~\kps. The central grid solution gives $Ω/Ω_{\rm c}=0.93$, $v_{\rm e}/v_{\rm c}=0.77$, $i=65^\circ$, $R_{\rm e}/R_{\rm p}=1.25$, and an equatorial centrifugal-to-gravitational acceleration ratio $η_{\rm e}=0.50$. Roche critical rotation requires $η_{\rm e}=1$ and $R_{\rm e}/R_{\rm p}=1.5$: despite the high angular rate, the central solution is not critical in equatorial force balance. The projected velocity exceeds, but is statistically consistent with, the previous spherical-fit value.} {\object{LAMOST J040643.69+542347.8} has a markedly oblate, gravity-darkened photosphere. Its proximity to critical rotation should be assessed using $Ω/Ω_{\rm c}$, $v_{\rm e}/v_{\rm c}$, and $η_{\rm e}$ together. A controlled spherical fit with the same atmosphere grid is needed to isolate the bias from neglecting deformation and gravity darkening.}

AI.tldr: Re-analysis of the O-type runaway LAMOST J040643.69+542347.8 with an oblate, gravity-darkened photospheric model yields markedly oblate parameters (Ω/Ωc=0.93, R_e/R_p=1.25) that are near- but not at critical rotation.
AI.motivation: Rapid rotation distorts massive stars, so parameters derived from spherical models become inclination-dependent and biased. The extreme Galactic O-type runaway LAMOST J040643.69+542347.8 is an ideal target to quantify these effects.
AI.method: Non-LTE oblate, gravity-darkened photospheric modelling with ZPEKTR, using TLUSTY/SYNSPEC emergent fluxes, limb darkening weighted over the visible Roche surface, Espinosa-Lara & Rieutord gravity darkening, and Schöning--Butler Stark profiles for selected He II lines; continuum-normalised spectra over 4000--4600 Å were fitted after masking interstellar and wind/circumstellar features.
AI.result: Model reproduces He II λ4200, He I λ4471, and He II λ4542. PNRC parameters: T_eff=38,716±1041 K, log g=4.12±0.12, v_e sin i=587±73 km/s. Central solution: Ω/Ωc=0.93, v_e/v_c=0.77, i=65°, R_e/R_p=1.25, η_e=0.50. Roche critical rotation would require η_e=1 and R_e/R_p=1.5, so the star is not critically rotating in equatorial force balance. v_e sin i exceeds but is statistically consistent with the previous spherical-fit value.
AI.conclusion: LAMOST J040643.69+542347.8 has a markedly oblate, gravity-darkened photosphere. Its proximity to critical rotation should be judged jointly via Ω/Ωc, v_e/v_c, and η_e. A controlled spherical fit with the same atmosphere grid is needed to isolate the bias from neglecting deformation and gravity darkening.

title: The M87 Black Hole Mass from JWST and Keck Stellar Kinematics Spanning 10 pc to 10 kpc
comment: 18 pages, 11 figures
summary: We combine JWST NIRSpec and Keck KCWI observations to construct a contiguous 2D map of M87's stellar kinematics spanning three decades in projected radius, from ${\sim}10$ pc to ${\sim}10$ kpc, and measure the mass of its central supermassive black hole. The innermost stellar kinematic measurements probe projected radii as small as ${\sim}3$% of the black hole's sphere of influence radius, or approximately 30,000 Schwarzschild radii. The NIRSpec spectra within $R < 0.45''$ are contaminated by quasiperiodic "wiggle" artifacts. We develop hyphen, which uses detector spectral traces to predict how the wiggle frequency varies with wavelength, then fits and subtracts the wiggle pattern from each spectrum in each exposure before combining the data. The cleaned spectra reveal a pronounced central rise in stellar velocity dispersion and $h_4$. Triaxial Schwarzschild stellar orbit modeling with the TriOS code, fitting ${\sim}$5,000 kinematic constraints across 618 spatial bins from JWST and Keck, yields a black hole mass of $M_{\mathrm{BH}}=(5.38 \pm 0.13\pm 0.22)\times10^9\,M_\odot$. This result is consistent with our prior KCWI-only determination but with the statistical uncertainty reduced by a factor of 2-3, now subdominant to the systematic uncertainty in the distance ($D$) to M87. Our inferred mass-to-distance ratio is $θ_g=GM_{\mathrm{BH}}/(c^2 D) = 3.16 \pm 0.08\, μ$as, whose 90% credible interval overlaps with that obtained from the multi-epoch Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) analysis, providing a robust and independent prior for future EHT studies.

AI.tldr: Combining JWST NIRSpec and Keck KCWI data with a new artifact-correction tool ("hyphen") and triaxial Schwarzschild orbit modeling, the authors measure M87's black hole mass to M_BH = (5.38 ± 0.13 ± 0.22) × 10^9 M_⊙, with statistical uncertainty now subdominant to distance systematics.
AI.motivation: Prior KCWI-only kinematics of M87 yielded a black hole mass but with limited statistical precision and only partial radial coverage. Extending spatially-resolved stellar kinematics down to very small projected radii—approaching the sphere of influence—can tighten the mass measurement, reduce statistical error, and provide an independent mass-to-distance ratio suitable as a prior for Event Horizon Telescope analyses.
AI.method: Contiguous 2D stellar kinematic map from ~10 pc to ~10 kpc using JWST NIRSpec plus Keck KCWI, reaching projected radii ~3% of the sphere of influence radius (~30,000 Schwarzschild radii). NIRSpec "wiggle" artifacts within R < 0.45'' are removed with a new tool, hyphen, which uses detector spectral traces to predict the wavelength dependence of the wiggle frequency and fits/subtracts the pattern per spectrum per exposure. Mass is inferred via triaxial Schwarzschild stellar orbit modeling (TriOS) fitting ~5,000 kinematic constraints across 618 spatial bins.
AI.result: Cleaned spectra show a pronounced central rise in velocity dispersion and h_4. TriOS modeling yields M_BH = (5.38 ± 0.13 ± 0.22) × 10^9 M_⊙, consistent with the prior KCWI-only value but with statistical uncertainty reduced by a factor of 2–3, now subdominant to the distance systematic. Mass-to-distance ratio θ_g = GM_BH/(c^2 D) = 3.16 ± 0.08 μas, whose 90% credible interval overlaps the multi-epoch EHT result.
AI.conclusion: JWST plus KCWI kinematics with proper artifact correction and triaxial orbit modeling provide a precise, statistically improved M87 black hole mass that is now limited by distance systematics, and deliver an independent θ_g consistent with EHT, serving as a robust prior for future EHT studies.

title: Photometric Study of a Distant SU UMa-type Dwarf Nova KSP-OT-201803a
comment: 10 pages, PASP accepted
summary: We present the discovery and photometric study of a distant dwarf nova KSP-OT-201803a using BVI-band observation data obtained by using the KMTNet Supernova Program. One superoutburst (SO) and three normal outbursts are identified from two years of observations (2018-2019), which show that KSP-OT-201803a is an SU UMa-type dwarf nova (DN). Applying the phase dispersion minimization method to the superhump data during the plateau phase of the SO yields a superhump period of P_sh = 127.4 minutes (=2.123 hr =0.08847 days). By stacking ten images of the quiescent phase, we find the quiescent phase magnitude of V = 22.59 +/- 0.18 mag. The SO shows quiescent-to-peak amplitude of 4.97 +/- 0.18 mag and duration of 16.59 days which are typical for the SU UMa-type DNe. Using the superhump period-orbital period relation of SU UMa stars, we obtain the approximate distance of 3.7 +/- 0.3 kpc to KSP-OT-201803a and Galactocentric distance of 9.4 kpc and height from the Galactic plane of +1.2 kpc. Stars at these large distances may belong to the Galactic halo or thick disk, which contain old, metal-poor Population II stars; therefore, these systems may have undergone a different evolutionary process than Population I objects. The orbital period gap of DNe spans 2.45-3.18 hours. Assuming that the orbital period of KSP-OT-201803a is a few percent shorter than its superhump period, KSP-OT-201803a may have just emerged from the period gap and recently resumed mass transfer after crossing its lower boundary.

AI.tldr: Discovery and photometric characterization of the distant SU UMa-type dwarf nova KSP-OT-201803a, with a 127.4-min superhump period, 4.97-mag outburst amplitude, and an estimated distance of 3.7 kpc placing it likely in the Galactic halo/thick disk.
AI.motivation: Dwarf novae at large Galactocentric distances and heights above the plane may belong to old, metal-poor Population II populations, potentially following a different evolutionary path than Population I systems; characterizing such distant DNe tests whether the standard disk-instability and angular-momentum-loss framework holds across stellar populations.
AI.method: BVI-band photometric monitoring with the KMTNet Supernova Program over two years (2018–2019), identifying one superoutburst and three normal outbursts. The phase dispersion minimization (PDM) method is applied to superhump data during the superoutburst plateau to derive P_sh. Quiescent magnitude is obtained by stacking ten images. Distance and Galactocentric coordinates are inferred via the superhump–orbital period relation for SU UMa stars.
AI.result: Superhump period P_sh = 127.4 min (2.123 hr, 0.08847 d); quiescent V = 22.59 ± 0.18 mag; outburst amplitude 4.97 ± 0.18 mag and duration 16.59 d, typical of SU UMa DNe. Derived distance 3.7 ± 0.3 kpc, Galactocentric distance 9.4 kpc, and height above the plane +1.2 kpc.
AI.conclusion: KSP-OT-201803a is confirmed as an SU UMa-type DN located in the Galactic halo or thick disk, possibly hosting an old, metal-poor donor. Assuming its orbital period is a few percent shorter than P_sh, the system likely sits just above the 2.45–3.18 hr period gap, having recently emerged from the gap and resumed mass transfer after crossing its lower boundary.

title: A pocket of oxygen in a near-pristine galaxy at z=4.2: chemical inhomogeneity at 10-parsec scales in LAP2
comment: 12 pages (7 figures, 1 table). Submitted to A&A
summary: We aim to constrain the oxygen abundance, the ionizing properties, and the spatial structure of LAP2, a strongly lensed (with a magnification $μ$~50) oxygen-deficient galaxy at z=4.2 behind the galaxy cluster Abell 2744. We present new JWST/NIRSpec IFU PRISM observations (~13.6 hr) of LAP2, which we combine with archival JWST/NIRCam imaging. LAP2 is intrinsically extremely faint (M_UV=-12.7) and has a low stellar mass (M~$10^5~M_\odot$), comparable to that of massive star clusters. It consists of a compact core ($R_{eff}$~7 pc) embedded in a more diffuse emission (with $R_{eff}$~20 pc). Strong H$α$ emission (EW$_{\rm rest}\simeq880$ Å, $\logξ_{\rm ion}\simeq25.3$), a blue UV slope ($β_{\rm UV}\simeq-2.5$, down to $\simeq-3.1$ in the core), and a Balmer decrement consistent with no dust attenuation indicate a young ($\lesssim10$ Myr), dust-free burst. [OIII]$λ$5007 is not detected in the integrated spectrum, implying [OIII]/H$β\leq0.61$ ($3σ$) and, using an extrapolated strong-line calibration, $12+\log({\rm O/H})\leq6.4$ ($\lesssim0.5\%\,Z_\odot$). This places LAP2 among the most metal-poor galaxies known. Faint [OIII] emission is, however, detected in the core (with $\rm4σ$ significance), where we derive $12+\log({\rm O/H})\simeq6.6$ ($\sim1\%\,Z_\odot$). This difference can be explained either by local self-enrichment, requiring only $\rm \sim0.2\,M_\odot$ of newly synthesized oxygen, or by a higher ionization parameter in the core. The upper limit on HeII$λ$1640 (EW$_{\rm rest}<39$ Å, $3σ$) does not exclude a contribution from metal-free stars. LAP2 extends the census of spectroscopically confirmed EMPGs to star-cluster masses and to $M_{\rm UV}\approx-13$. Its location in a low-density region supports a scenario in which underdense environments preserve nearly pristine gas well after reionization.

AI.tldr: JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of the strongly lensed (μ~50) z=4.2 galaxy LAP2 reveal an extremely metal-poor (12+log(O/H)≤6.4, ≲0.5% Z⊙), intrinsically faint (M_UV=-12.7), low-mass (M~10^5 M⊙), dust-free young starburst with a compact core embedded in diffuse emission, in a low-density environment.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to constrain the oxygen abundance, ionizing properties, and spatial structure of LAP2, an oxygen-deficient strongly lensed galaxy at z=4.2. Such extreme emission-line, metal-poor galaxies (EMPGs) probe early chemical enrichment and the nature of ionizing sources, but are difficult to characterize without lensing magnification and deep spectroscopy.
AI.method: New JWST/NIRSpec IFU PRISM observations (~13.6 hr) of LAP2 behind Abell 2744, combined with archival JWST/NIRCam imaging. Integrated and spatially resolved spectroscopy yields Hα, UV slope β, Balmer decrement, [OIII]λ5007 limits/detections, the ionization parameter, and a HeIIλ1640 upper limit, from which metallicity and structure are derived.
AI.result: LAP2 is intrinsically very faint (M_UV=-12.7) and low mass (M~10^5 M⊙), with a compact core (R_eff~7 pc) in diffuse emission (R_eff~20 pc). Strong Hα (EW_rest≃880 Å, logξ_ion≃25.3), blue UV slope (β_UV≃-2.5, down to -3.1 in the core), and a dust-free Balmer decrement indicate a young (≲10 Myr) burst. Integrated [OIII]λ5007 is undetected ([OIII]/Hβ≤0.61, 3σ), giving 12+log(O/H)≤6.4 (≲0.5% Z⊙). Faint [OIII] (4σ) in the core yields 12+log(O/H)≃6.6 (~1% Z⊙). HeIIλ1640 upper limit (EW_rest<39 Å, 3σ) does not exclude metal-free stellar contributions.
AI.conclusion: LAP2 is among the most metal-poor galaxies known, extending the confirmed EMPG census to star-cluster masses and M_UV≈-13. The integrated-core metallicity difference is attributable to local self-enrichment (~0.2 M⊙ of new oxygen) or a higher core ionization parameter. Its low-density environment supports a scenario in which underdense regions preserve nearly pristine gas well after reionization.

title: Frequent Optical Flares in an M-type Detached Eclipsing Binary TIC 349005337
comment: 20 pages, 11 figures, 9 tables; accepted by ApJ
summary: A comprehensive photometric and spectroscopic analysis of TIC 349005337, a highly active M-type detached eclipsing binary with an orbital period of 2.6079133 days, is presented utilizing high-cadence and long-term monitoring photometry from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) and medium-resolution spectroscopy from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST). By integrating radial velocity curves with light curves, we determined the fundamental physical parameters for both components. The system consists of an M-dwarf primary ($M_1 = 0.517 \pm 0.009 M_\odot$, $R_1 = 0.518 \pm 0.003 R_\odot$) and a fully convective secondary ($M_2 = 0.298 \pm 0.004 M_\odot$, $R_2 = 0.357 \pm 0.003 R_\odot$). A total of 12 high-energy stellar flares, with the most energetic event reaching $3.87 \times 10^{34}$ erg, is identified, confirming the system is in a state of magnetic hyper-activity. The frequent superflares suggest that intense magnetic activity and significant starspot coverage play a dominant role in altering the stellar atmospheric structure. As the secondary component falls below the fully convective boundary, these energetic flares provide critical empirical constraints for distributed dynamo models in the low-mass regime. Our results highlight TIC 349005337 as an ideal laboratory for investigating the interplay between binary dynamics, magnetic reconnection, and the resulting impact on the atmospheric stability of potential orbiting exoplanets.

AI.tldr: A complete photometric/spectroscopic study of the active M-dwarf detached eclipsing binary TIC 349005337, determining component masses/radii and characterizing 12 superflares.
AI.motivation: Low-mass M-dwarf binaries with strong magnetic activity are rare benchmarks for testing stellar structure and dynamo models, yet well-characterized systems with precise fundamental parameters and flare statistics are scarce; the fully convective secondary offers a test of distributed dynamo theory.
AI.method: Combined high-cadence, long-baseline TESS photometry with medium-resolution LAMOST spectroscopy; jointly modeled radial-velocity curves and light curves (period 2.6079133 d) to derive absolute parameters; identified and energetically characterized flares from TESS light curves.
AI.result: Primary: M1=0.517±0.009 Msun, R1=0.518±0.003 Rsun; secondary: M2=0.298±0.004 Msun, R2=0.357±0.003 Rsun. Twelve high-energy flares detected, the strongest at 3.87×10^34 erg, indicating magnetic hyper-activity and substantial starspot coverage; the secondary lies below the fully convective boundary.
AI.conclusion: TIC 349005337 is a magnetic hyper-active M-dwarf binary whose superflares constrain distributed dynamo models in the low-mass regime and serve as a laboratory for binary dynamics, magnetic reconnection, and atmospheric stability of potential exoplanets.

title: She Sees Shells by the Stellar Shore: A Kinematic View of NGC 253's Stellar Halo
comment: 33 pages, 12 figures, accepted to ApJ
summary: The stellar halos of nearby galaxies are fossil records of ancient mergers, providing insight into the formation and growth of these systems. These halos often contain substructure in the form of streams, shells, and debris fields that make up dynamically young remnants of past accretions. These remnants can be probed with resolved-star spectroscopic observations, giving insight into the kinematics of bygone satellite companions. Such observations have been made for the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda, but are much more challenging and expensive to do outside the Local Group. The Local Volume has an abundance of MW-mass galaxies with richly structured halos, such as NGC 253. Leveraging the power of Magellan's M2FS fiber-fed multiobject spectrograph, we have obtained medium-resolution spectra of 225 stars centered on NGC 253's southwestern shell. These spectra enabled us to make the first-ever measurement of the resolved-star stellar kinematics for 89 stars in NGC 253's halo. We also detect substructure in several ways and identify regions likely to be accreted and in-situ, finding among them a low-velocity region coincident with the previously reported SW shell we believe was accreted recently, and an in-situ component that traces the outer disk. After subtracting NGC 253's systemic velocity, we measure median line-of-sight velocities of $-34_{-12}^{+16}$ km/s and $167_{-14}^{+16}$ km/s for the accreted and in-situ populations, respectively. This work highlights the utility of kinematics to differentiate between accreted and in-situ stars, and acts as a pathfinder for future observations with next-generation 30 m telescopes and wide-field multiobject spectrographs.

AI.tldr: First resolved-star kinematic measurement of NGC 253's southwestern shell using M2FS, separating accreted and in-situ halo populations.
AI.motivation: Stellar halos are fossil records of ancient mergers, but resolved-star kinematics outside the Local Group are scarce and expensive; NGC 253 in the Local Volume offers an accessible richly structured halo.
AI.method: Magellan/M2FS medium-resolution multi-object spectroscopy of 225 stars centered on the SW shell; resolved-star stellar kinematics for 89 halo stars; substructure detection and accreted/in-situ classification.
AI.result: Substructure detected; a low-velocity region coincident with the SW shell is identified as recently accreted, and an in-situ component traces the outer disk. After systemic-velocity subtraction, median line-of-sight velocities are -34 (-12/+16) km/s (accreted) and 167 (-14/+16) km/s (in-situ).
AI.conclusion: Kinematics effectively distinguish accreted from in-situ stars; the work is a pathfinder for future 30 m telescopes and wide-field multi-object spectrographs.

title: Collective Characterization of Polar Crown Filament Eruptions
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: Polar crown filaments (PCFs) are crucially related to the structure of solar polar magnetic fields. They are physically significant because of the ``rush-to-the-pole'' motion, which is an indicator of the poleward drift of magnetic fields from decayed active regions. The formation and evolution of PCFs offer important insights into the Sun's magnetic activity at high latitudes and the solar cycle variation. In this study, we present a collective analysis of 50 PCF disappearance events covering solar cycle 24 and 25. Among them, 24 show rotational motions, and nine have sufficiently clear magnetic configurations for comparison with numerical model predictions. In all nine events, the observed rotation directions agree with the model predictions, suggesting possible magnetic-flux-rope-like structures in these events. All except one of the PCFs in our sample disappeared through eruption rather than thermal disappearance, and most associated CMEs were slow ($<800$ km s$^{-1}$). For events accompanied by transient coronal holes, the estimated magnetic flux associated with the dimming regions is on the order of $10^{20}$--$10^{21}$ Mx. Time--distance analysis identifies 22 events with a clear slow-rise to fast-rise transition, with onset heights ranging from several tens to about 160 Mm and a mean onset velocity of about 2.8 km s$^{-1}$ after excluding the highest-velocity event. Together, these findings characterize the magnetic structure and dynamics of PCF eruptions.

AI.tldr: Collective analysis of 50 polar crown filament disappearance events across solar cycles 24-25: rotation directions match flux-rope model predictions in all 9 testable cases, nearly all disappear via eruption (mostly slow CMEs), with quantified flux and slow-to-fast rise onset properties.
AI.motivation: PCFs are tied to polar magnetic field structure and the "rush-to-the-pole" poleward drift of decayed active-region fields, so their formation/evolution informs high-latitude magnetic activity and solar cycle variation; a systematic multi-event characterization was lacking.
AI.method: Statistical sample study of 50 PCF disappearance events spanning solar cycles 24 and 25; identification of rotational motions; comparison of observed rotation directions with numerical model predictions for 9 events with clear magnetic configurations; classification of disappearance mechanism (eruption vs. thermal); CME speed cataloging; magnetic flux estimation for transient coronal hole/dimming regions; time-distance analysis of rise profiles.
AI.result: 24/50 events show rotational motion; 9 have configurations clear enough for model comparison and all 9 rotation directions agree with predictions, suggesting flux-rope-like structures. All but one PCF disappeared via eruption, with most associated CMEs slow (<800 km/s). Dimming-region flux ~10^20-10^21 Mx. 22 events show clear slow-rise to fast-rise transitions, onset heights from tens of Mm to ~160 Mm, mean onset velocity ~2.8 km/s (excluding the fastest event).
AI.conclusion: PCF eruptions are predominantly eruptive, slow-CME-associated events consistent with magnetic-flux-rope structures; the quantified rotation, flux, and rise-onset properties collectively characterize PCF magnetic structure and dynamics and support their use as tracers of polar field evolution.

title: ReveaLLAGN 2: Exploring the Nuclear Gas and Stellar Kinematics of Nearby LLAGNs with JWST/NIRSpec IFU
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Low-luminosity active galactic nuclei (LLAGN) represent the most common mode of black hole accretion in the local Universe, yet their nuclear structure, stellar and gas kinematics remain poorly constrained at parsec scales. We investigate the nuclear regions of eight nearby representative LLAGN, the ReveaLLAGN sample: M87, M104, M94, M81, NGC1052, NGC4258, NGC5128 and NGC4395. Using JWST/NIRSpec data, we probe the stellar, molecular hydrogen, hydrogen recombination, and high ionisation coronal lines kinematics and their spatial distribution, exploring how detectability and spatial distributions of these lines vary across different Eddington ratios. The stellar LOSV maps reveal a slowly rotating disk in the nuclei of all our targets, characterised by an anti-correlation with the h3 Gauss-Hermite moment. Across the sample, the stellar velocity dispersion rises toward the central black hole. Only in M104 and M94 does the velocity dispersion display a more intricate pattern that departs from a simple disk configuration, indicating the presence of multiple kinematic components in these galaxies. Across the sample, the gas distribution and kinematics exhibit rotation that is frequently decoupled from the stellar rotation, suggesting that the stellar gravitational potential is decoupled from the current accretion state. The gas kinematics are often visually aligned with the radio jet, presenting broader velocity dispersions along the jet direction. Line-ratio maps indicate that the dominant excitation mechanism is photoionisation by the central AGN, with mechanical heating from shocks becoming important only at higher Eddington ratios. Across the sample, we detect coronal lines in all LLAGN when using nuclear-aperture spectra, and we can obtain spatially resolved kinematics only in NGC5128 and NGC4395, the highest Eddington ratio sources.

AI.tldr: JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of eight nearby low-luminosity AGN (ReveaLLAGN sample) reveal slowly rotating nuclear stellar disks with central velocity-dispersion peaks, gas kinematics frequently decoupled from the stars and often aligned with radio jets, AGN photoionization as the dominant excitation mechanism, and coronal lines detectable in nuclear apertures for all targets but spatially resolved only in the two highest Eddington-ratio sources.
AI.motivation: LLAGN are the most common accretion mode in the local Universe, but their parsec-scale nuclear structure and stellar/gas kinematics are poorly constrained. The study aims to characterize these properties across a representative sample and link line detectability and spatial distribution to Eddington ratio.
AI.method: Analysis of JWST/NIRSpec integral-field spectroscopy of eight nearby LLAGN (M87, M104, M94, M81, NGC1052, NGC4258, NGC5128, NGC4395). Stellar kinematics are derived via line-of-sight velocity (LOSV) maps and Gauss-Hermite moments (h3); molecular hydrogen, hydrogen recombination and high-ionization coronal line kinematics and spatial distributions are mapped and compared with radio jet orientation. Line-ratio (diagnostic) maps are used to identify the dominant excitation mechanism, and detectability is assessed as a function of Eddington ratio.
AI.result: Stellar LOSV maps show a slowly rotating disk in all nuclei, anti-correlated with h3. Stellar velocity dispersion rises toward the central black hole; only M104 and M94 show more complex, non-disk-like dispersion patterns indicating multiple kinematic components. Gas rotation is frequently decoupled from stellar rotation, implying the stellar gravitational potential is decoupled from the current accretion state. Gas kinematics are often visually aligned with the radio jet, with broader velocity dispersions along the jet direction. Line-ratio maps indicate AGN photoionization dominates, with shock/mechanical heating becoming important only at higher Eddington ratios. Coronal lines are detected in nuclear-aperture spectra for all targets but spatially resolved only in NGC5128 and NGC4395, the highest Eddington-ratio sources.
AI.conclusion: Parsec-scale NIRSpec kinematics of LLAGN reveal a common slowly rotating stellar disk with central dispersion peaks, but gas kinematics largely decoupled from the stars and shaped by jet-related and accretion-state effects. AGN photoionization dominates excitation across the sample, with shocks contributing at high Eddington ratios, and coronal-line spatial resolution is limited to the highest Eddington-ratio nuclei, linking observability of the AGN-driven gas to accretion efficiency.

title: Tiny Quiet-Sun EUV Ejections Revealed by High-resolution Multiwavelength Observations
summary: We investigate two successive tiny quiet-Sun EUV ejections on 2022 October 29 using coordinated Solar Orbiter/EUI, IRIS, SDO/AIA, and Goode Solar Telescope observations. We examine their low-lying geometry and the chromospheric and transition-region response before and between the releases. A curved H-alpha thread is present beforehand, and Mg ii and Si iv spectra reveal a compact multithermal precursor 2.6--2.7 min before the first EUV brightening. EUI--AIA stereoscopy places the recurrent compact EUV kernel near 2.2 Mm and the sampled emission at approximately 0.6--4.2 Mm along inclined, locally arched structures. The first ejection shows multithreaded, helical-looking EUV strands; the second shows straighter strands and a decrease in the cross-ridge separation of redshifted and blueshifted Mg ii k3 samples from 1.47'' to 0.89''. Nevertheless, the two peaks have comparable emission-measure increments and estimated event-associated thermal contents of a few 10^26 erg under the same assumptions. Before the second ejection, the regional Si iv and k3 blueshift signals remain enhanced, while the Mg ii central reversal along the activated ridge remains shallower than before the event. Component reconnection between the curved structure and the surrounding field offers a possible explanation. The observations show that jet-like EUV emission can occur in low-lying structures. The second ejection begins before the chromospheric and transition-region spectra have returned to their pre-event states. Its spectral signatures may therefore depend on the atmospheric changes associated with the first ejection as well as on the additional energy input.

AI.tldr: Two successive tiny quiet-Sun EUV ejections are studied with multi-instrument observations, revealing a low-lying curved H-alpha thread, a multithermal precursor, and a second ejection that begins before the atmosphere recovers from the first.
AI.motivation: To understand the low-lying geometry and chromospheric/transition-region response of tiny quiet-Sun EUV ejections before and between successive releases, and how recurrent ejections interact with a pre-conditioned atmosphere.
AI.method: Coordinated Solar Orbiter/EUI, IRIS (Mg ii and Si iv spectra), SDO/AIA, and Goode Solar Telescope (H-alpha) observations of two successive ejections on 2022 Oct 29, combined with EUI-AIA stereoscopy and spectral diagnostics (k3 Doppler shifts, central reversal depth, emission measure).
AI.result: A curved H-alpha thread precedes the events, with a compact multithermal precursor 2.6-2.7 min before the first EUV brightening. Stereoscopy places the recurrent kernel near 2.2 Mm and sampled emission ~0.6-4.2 Mm along inclined arched structures. The first ejection shows multithreaded, helical-looking strands; the second shows straighter strands with reduced cross-ridge separation of redshifted/blueshifted k3 samples (1.47'' to 0.89''). Both peaks have comparable emission-measure increments and thermal contents of a few 10^26 erg.
AI.conclusion: Jet-like EUV emission can arise in low-lying structures. The second ejection begins before the chromosphere and transition region return to pre-event states, so its spectral signatures may depend both on atmospheric changes from the first ejection and on additional energy input. Component reconnection between the curved structure and surrounding field is a plausible mechanism.

title: DESI DR2 Results III: The Mass of the Milky Way
comment: This paper is a DESI Collaboration Key Project publication. 25+12 pages, 14+2 figures, 5+1 tables. Submitted to ApJ
summary: We present measurements of the mass of the Milky Way using distant halo stars selected from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 (DR2). We apply four dynamical modeling methods to 10,036 RR Lyrae (RRL) and blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars with 6D phase space coordinates that span from $\sim$10 to 95 kpc from the Galactic center, the largest samples of their kind. All methods are applied to mock surveys based on cosmological simulations that include generating individual tracer stars, convolving their phase-space coordinates with DESI and Gaia DR3-like uncertainties, and tailored models of the survey selection functions. By comparing the performance on these mocks, we quantify how systematic biases from both methodology assumptions and galaxy disequilibrium impact each estimate. The mock-based systematics, which differ by method and tracer, are used to correct the individual estimates and to derive joint estimates using a rigorous formalism that accounts for per-method biases and residual correlations between methods. We obtain a joint estimate of the mass within 80 kpc to be $M(r < 80 \mathrm{\,kpc}) = 6.36^{+0.53}_{-0.48} \times 10^{11}$ M$_\odot$ and a virial mass estimate of $M_\mathrm{200c} = 1.19^{+0.14}_{-0.12} \times 10^{12}$ M$_\odot$, with similar results when combining only RRL-based or BHB-based measurements. These results provide a roadmap for future DESI efforts, as well as those in other spectroscopic surveys, to reliably constrain the mass of our Galaxy.

AI.tldr: The authors measure the Milky Way's mass using 10,036 RR Lyrae and blue horizontal branch halo stars from DESI DR2, applying four dynamical methods calibrated on cosmological mock surveys to derive a joint mass estimate with quantified systematics.
AI.motivation: Precise Milky Way mass measurements are hampered by systematic biases from modeling assumptions and galaxy disequilibrium, which are rarely quantified in a consistent framework.
AI.method: Four dynamical modeling methods are applied to 10,036 RR Lyrae and BHB stars with 6D phase-space coordinates spanning ~10–95 kpc (largest samples of their kind). Each method is validated on mock surveys built from cosmological simulations, including individual tracer generation, convolution with DESI and Gaia DR3-like uncertainties, and tailored selection functions. Mock-derived per-method systematics are used to correct individual estimates and to compute joint estimates via a formalism accounting for per-method biases and residual inter-method correlations.
AI.result: Joint mass within 80 kpc: M(r < 80 kpc) = 6.36^{+0.53}_{-0.48} × 10^11 M_sun; virial mass M_200c = 1.19^{+0.14}_{-0.12} × 10^12 M_sun, with consistent results using only RRL or only BHB samples.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a systematic-bias-corrected, multi-method framework and a roadmap for future DESI and other spectroscopic surveys to reliably constrain the Milky Way's mass.

title: Spectroscopic diagnostics of coronal fan loops using EIS/Hinode and AIA/SDO
comment: 13 pages, 13 figures
summary: We utilize spectroscopic and imaging data from the EIS/Hinode and the AIA/SDO to determine plasma and wave parameters along coronal fan loops. We determined the temperature along the loop lengths using the EM-loci method with EIS spectral lines and identified multi-thermal plasma components at temperatures ranging from 0.8-1.05, 1.2-1.4, and 1.6-1.8 MK. We further compared these temperature distributions along the loops with those derived from DEM analysis carried out using AIA coronal passbands. The multi-thermal nature of coronal fan loops can be well resolved using EIS spectroscopic data. We determined the density along the loop using the line-ratio method from the EIS Fe XII line pair. We found that density decreases slowly from the expected hydrostatic equilibrium. Our results demonstrate the multi-thermal nature of overdense loops, which can be well resolved with EIS spectroscopic data. We also determined the velocity amplitude of Alfvén waves from the non-thermal broadening of EIS Fe XII spectral line profiles. We further estimated the Alfvén wave energy flux in the corona by combining these parameters with the recently reported magnetic field strength of $\approx$200 G at the coronal footpoint of fan loops. The estimated Alfvén wave energy flux is $\approx$ 2$\times 10^7$ erg cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, significantly higher than those reported in earlier studies, and can contribute to coronal losses due to radiation along the fan loops in the active region.

AI.tldr: Using EIS/Hinode spectroscopy and AIA/SDO imaging, the authors characterize coronal fan loops as multi-thermal, overdense structures with a slowly declining density and show that their Alfvén wave energy flux (~2×10^7 erg cm^-2 s^-1) can supply coronal radiative losses.
AI.motivation: The thermal structure, density, and wave-driven energy budget of coronal fan loops in active regions are poorly constrained; earlier Alfvén wave flux estimates were likely too low, so a combined spectroscopic and imaging determination of plasma and wave parameters is needed to test whether waves can balance coronal losses.
AI.method: EM-loci analysis of EIS spectral lines to derive loop temperatures and identify multi-thermal components (0.8–1.05, 1.2–1.4, 1.6–1.8 MK), cross-checked against AIA-based DEM analysis; electron density from the EIS Fe XII line-ratio diagnostics; velocity amplitude of Alfvén waves from non-thermal broadening of Fe XII profiles; and Alfvén wave energy flux estimated by combining these with a magnetic field strength of ≈200 G at the loop footpoints.
AI.result: Multi-thermal plasma components are clearly resolved by EIS spectroscopy and consistent with AIA DEM results; density decreases more slowly than expected for hydrostatic equilibrium, indicating overdense loops; the derived Alfvén wave energy flux is ≈2×10^7 erg cm^-2 s^-1, significantly higher than earlier reported values.
AI.conclusion: Coronal fan loops are multi-thermal and overdense, and the inferred Alfvén wave energy flux is sufficient to contribute substantially to coronal radiative losses along the fan loops in the active region.

title: Mock catalogues for the DESI DR2 Milky Way mass modeling effort
comment: This paper is a DESI Collaboration Key Project publication. 13+4 pages, 9+0 figures, 0+2 tables. Submitted to The Open Journal of Astrophysics, comments welcome
summary: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) survey is an ongoing campaign to obtain millions of spectra, including for stars within the Milky Way. One of DESI's Key Projects for its second data release (DR2) is to measure the mass of the Milky Way using a variety of techniques applied to six-dimensional kinematics of distant halo stars. We present mock surveys generated from the Auriga cosmological simulations (AuriDESI) that are used to validate these techniques in several companion studies. The AuriDESI tracer catalogues are tailored to reflect key features of the DR2 Key Project dataset, including the selection of RR Lyrae and blue horizontal branch stars, uncertainties on line-of-sight velocities and proper motions, and variation in observational completeness within the survey footprint. We discuss how well the resulting AuriDESI tracer catalogues compare to their observed DESI counterparts, including suggesting improvements that can be generalized to similar mock survey efforts within the community. The AuriDESI tracer catalogues are publicly available on Zenodo.

AI.tldr: AuriDESI provides mock DESI-like surveys from Auriga cosmological simulations to validate Milky Way mass-measurement techniques for DR2.
AI.motivation: DESI's DR2 Key Project aims to measure the Milky Way mass using 6D kinematics of distant halo stars; these techniques require validation against controlled, realistic mock datasets.
AI.method: Mock surveys (AuriDESI) are generated from Auriga cosmological simulations, with tracer catalogues tailored to reproduce key DESI features: RR Lyrae and blue horizontal branch selection, line-of-sight velocity and proper-motion uncertainties, and spatially varying observational completeness across the survey footprint.
AI.result: AuriDESI tracer catalogues are compared with their observed DESI counterparts, assessing fidelity and identifying suggested improvements generalizable to similar mock survey efforts.
AI.conclusion: AuriDESI mock catalogues serve as a validation foundation for companion Milky Way mass studies and are publicly released on Zenodo.

title: Magnetism among the oldest white dwarfs in the solar neighbourhood
comment: Accepted by MNRAS
summary: We present a new circular polarisation survey of approximately 100 white dwarfs selected as featureless DC stars and combine our measurements with previous observations. Our compilation contains 205 objects, of which 24 show firm circular polarisation detections, while another four show marginal signals that require confirmation. Four magnetic white dwarfs originally classified as DC show polarisation spectra with significant contributions from spectral lines. Depending on the treatment of these objects and of the marginal detections, the inferred fraction of magnetic objects in the DC selected sample lies between approximately 10 and 14%. Among objects without identifiable line contributions, the circular polarisation never exceeds approximately 2%, substantially below the levels observed in some hotter magnetic white dwarfs with prominent spectral features. This is unlikely a symptom of field decay, since in our sample we find no significant evidence for a dependence of magnetic incidence on cooling age, and magnetic fields are detected in stars with cooling ages exceeding 9 Gyr. Instead, strong spectral line opacity provides a natural mechanism for producing much larger polarisation amplitudes than the continuum. In the full sample considered here, the incidence of detectable magnetism increases with stellar mass. Most average-mass magnetic stars for which repeated observations are available show no clear polarimetric variability, whereas variability appears more common among the most massive objects.

AI.tldr: A new circular spectropolarimetric survey of ~100 DC white dwarfs, combined with prior data (205 objects total), finds firm circular polarisation in 24 stars and marginal signals in 4, implying a magnetic fraction of ~10–14% among DC-selected white dwarfs; magnetism shows no dependence on cooling age, increases with stellar mass, and large polarisation amplitudes are attributed to line opacity rather than field strength.
AI.motivation: Featureless DC white dwarfs are difficult to diagnose magnetically because weak or absent line opacity limits conventional field detection, so the true incidence of magnetism and its dependence on cooling age, mass, and field evolution in this poorly characterised population remains uncertain.
AI.method: Circular spectropolarimetry of approximately 100 white dwarfs selected as featureless DC stars, compiled with previous observations into a sample of 205 objects; statistical analysis of magnetic incidence as a function of cooling age and stellar mass, plus tests for polarimetric variability from repeated observations.
AI.result: 24 firm circular polarisation detections and 4 marginal signals; inferred magnetic fraction of ~10–14% in the DC-selected sample. Four objects originally classified as DC show significant line contributions in their polarisation spectra. Among objects without identifiable line contributions, circular polarisation never exceeds ~2%. No significant dependence of magnetic incidence on cooling age, with fields detected in stars older than 9 Gyr. Magnetic incidence increases with stellar mass. Most average-mass magnetic stars show no clear polarimetric variability, whereas variability is more common among the most massive objects.
AI.conclusion: The low polarisation amplitudes in line-free DC stars are not evidence of field decay; instead, strong spectral line opacity is the natural mechanism producing much larger polarisation amplitudes than the continuum. Magnetism in DC white dwarfs is common (~10–14%), persists to old cooling ages, and is preferentially associated with higher masses.

title: Constraining the Milky Way Mass profile with data driven distribution function using DESI DR2 halo stars
comment: 23 pages, 11 figures. This paper is a DESI Collaboration Key Project publication
summary: We employ a novel data-driven dynamical modeling method, the empirical distribution function (emPDF), to constrain the Milky Way mass profile using a large sample of halo stars from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Milky Way Survey (DESI MWS). The method does not assume any functional form of the tracer distribution. Deviations from the steady-state assumption and the effects of observational errors are further tested and calibrated using a number of realistic mock observations (AuriDESI). Applying the calibrated method to two classes of tracers in DESI, we derive a best-constrained virial mass and concentration of $\log M_\mathrm{200c}/M_{\odot}=12.05_{-0.12}^{+0.21}(_{-0.18}^{+0.26})$ and $\log c_\mathrm{200c}=1.20_{-0.16}^{+0.11}(_{-0.24}^{+0.20})$ for BHBs. For RR Lyrae stars we derive $\log M_\mathrm{200c}/M_{\odot}=12.15_{-0.14}^{+0.22}(_{-0.19}^{+0.26})$ and $\log c_\mathrm{200c}=1.16_{-0.12}^{+0.09}(_{-0.18}^{+0.16})$. The uncertainties quoted outside and within brackets are statistical and total errors including systematic errors calibrated from AuriDESI, respectively. The two tracer populations provide overall consistent measurements of the MW halo mass profile. Combining the halo star constraints with the independent constraint from satellite dynamics, we derive a robust and precise final measurement of the MW halo parameters of $\log M_\mathrm{200c}/M_{\odot}=12.12_{-0.05}^{+0.05}(_{-0.04}^{+0.06})$ and $\log c_\mathrm{200c}=1.16_{-0.03}^{+0.05}(_{-0.07}^{+0.05})$, with correlation coefficients of $ρ=-0.90(-0.54)$.

AI.tldr: Using a novel data-driven emPDF dynamical modeling method calibrated with mock observations, this work constrains the Milky Way halo mass profile from DESI MWS halo stars, finding consistent results across tracers and a robust combined measurement of virial mass and concentration.
AI.motivation: Constraining the Milky Way mass profile typically relies on assuming functional forms for the tracer distribution; a method free of such assumptions, with calibrated systematics, is needed to obtain robust halo mass and concentration measurements from large spectroscopic samples.
AI.method: Employs the empirical distribution function (emPDF), a data-driven dynamical modeling technique that assumes no functional form for the tracer distribution. Systematics from deviations from steady state and observational errors are tested and calibrated using realistic AuriDESI mock observations. The calibrated method is applied to two tracer classes (BHB and RR Lyrae stars) from DESI MWS, and combined with an independent satellite-dynamics constraint.
AI.conclusion: The two DESI tracer populations give consistent Milky Way halo mass profiles, and combining halo-star constraints with satellite dynamics produces a precise, robust final measurement of the MW virial mass and concentration, with total errors calibrated from AuriDESI mocks.

title: Population synthesis of substellar companions surviving common-envelope evolution
comment: submitted to A&A
summary: Predicting the population of substellar companions around white dwarfs (WDs) requires accounting for both companions that avoid engulfment during stellar evolution and those that survive common-envelope (CE) evolution. While the former population was investigated in our previous population-synthesis study, a comprehensive population synthesis of the latter remains lacking. We investigated the fate of engulfed substellar companions within the same population-synthesis framework. We aim to predict the occurrence rates and properties of companions surviving CE evolution, identify the conditions permitting survival, and assess their detectability. We determined the stellar structure at the onset of CE evolution and calculated CE outcomes for different ejection efficiencies considering gravitational and thermal energy or the full internal energy of the envelope. Survival is rare and strongly depends on the evolutionary stage at engulfment. No companions entering CE evolution during the red-giant branch or early asymptotic-giant branch survive. Survivors originate exclusively from the thermally pulsing asymptotic-giant branch, when stellar envelopes can become weakly bound, allowing even relatively low-mass companions to survive. The resulting systems typically have orbital periods of a few hours. We predict occurrence rates of up to 0.16% among WDs, corresponding to an upper limit of 2.53 companions to WDs within 50 pc. Transit detection is primarily limited by orbital geometry, whereas all predicted survivors would produce detectable infrared excess with JWST out to 50pc. We predict that CE evolution produces a small but observable population of close substellar companions to WDs. Survival is governed not only by companion mass but critically by the envelope structure at engulfment, particularly during thermal pulses, and by the contribution of recombination energy to envelope ejection.

AI.tldr: A population-synthesis study predicts that substellar companions can survive common-envelope evolution around white dwarfs only when engulfed during the thermally pulsing AGB phase, yielding close (few-hour period) systems with occurrence rates up to 0.16% of WDs, detectable via JWST infrared excess.
AI.motivation: Previous work addressed companions that avoid engulfment; a comprehensive population synthesis of companions surviving common-envelope (CE) evolution had not been performed, so the fate, survival conditions, and detectability of engulfed substellar companions remained unquantified.
AI.method: Within the same population-synthesis framework, the authors determined stellar structure at the onset of CE evolution and computed CE outcomes for different ejection efficiencies, considering either gravitational plus thermal energy or the full internal energy of the envelope (including recombination energy).
AI.result: Survival is rare and depends strongly on the evolutionary stage at engulfment: no companions engulfed on the red-giant branch or early AGB survive. Survivors arise exclusively from the thermally pulsing AGB, where weakly bound envelopes allow even relatively low-mass companions to survive; systems typically have orbital periods of a few hours. Occurrence rates reach up to 0.16% among WDs (upper limit of 2.53 companions within 50 pc). Transit detection is limited mainly by orbital geometry, whereas all predicted survivors produce detectable infrared excess with JWST out to 50 pc.
AI.conclusion: CE evolution yields a small but observable population of close substellar companions to WDs. Survival is governed not only by companion mass but critically by envelope structure at engulfment (especially during thermal pulses) and by the contribution of recombination energy to envelope ejection.

title: A distribution-function estimate of the Milky Way mass profile from outer halo stars in DESI DR2
comment: This paper is a DESI Collaboration Key Project publication. To be submitted to OJAp. 23 pages, 11 figures
summary: We present measurements of the Milky Way mass using blue horizontal-branch (BHB) and RR Lyrae (RRL) stars from the second data release of DESI (DR2), covering its first three years of operations. We employ 279 BHBs and 213 RRLs at $\sim\!50$--$80$\,kpc from the Galactic center, selected from catalogs roughly twice as large as those of DESI DR1, used in our previous mass measurement. We apply the Galactic Mass Estimator (GME), a hierarchical Bayesian framework that assumes power-law forms for the potential and the tracer density, and accounts for distance and velocity uncertainties.
